name: Ximena Daugaard-Okonkwo
description:
Ximena is compact and strong for her age, with deep reddish-brown skin perpetually smudged with lubricant and composite dust. She keeps her hair in two thick plaits that she tucks into her collar when working and her hands are already showing the slight callus-thickening of someone who has used tools since she was eight. She has a bioluminescent birthmark — a faint greenish patch along her right collarbone, natural, not modded — that glows slightly in low light and which her coworkers call her 'running light.' She wears salvaged Ferrogate Transit safety goggles pushed up on her forehead like a permanent crown.

Ximena is formally registered as an apprentice with the Geartown Forge Collective under a provision that technically requires parental consent, which her uncle signed for. She earns Φ40/month — supplement to her household's UBC — doing frame alignment, bolt torque checks, and increasingly complex hydraulic diagnostics that her supervisor Adebowale trusts her with because she makes fewer errors than the adult apprentices. She is serious about the work with a seriousness that occasionally breaks into a very young, loud laugh when something surprises her.

core_fears: the Forge Collective losing its Ferrogate contract and her losing the apprenticeship
turning out to have less talent than she thinks
core_desires: to design something, not just maintain it
to make enough that her uncle doesn't have to work the late shift
coping_mechanisms: focusing intensely on one physical task until the anxiety recedes
talking to equipment while she works
blind_spots: doesn't see her supervisor's favoritism as potentially complicated — she reads it as purely meritocratic
has absorbed a contempt for non-technical work that she doesn't examine
psychology.secret: She found a design flaw in a Ferrogate transit car's braking assembly three months ago. She fixed it and said nothing because she was afraid reporting it officially would trigger an investigation that would expose how many hours she's actually working. If it hadn't been fixed, the car would eventually have failed.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: technical vocabulary far above her age; conversational speech is choppy and concrete; uncomfortable with abstraction
speech_patterns.cadence: short declarative sentences in sequence; trails off mid-sentence only when thinking through a problem
verbal_tics: 'the math works out' to mean 'I agree'
names tools in sentences where other people would use pronouns
example_lines: 'The math works out on going early. Get the torque wrench warmed up before the cold bolts.'
'Everybody talks about it like it's complicated. It's not complicated. Three moving parts. You understand three moving parts, you understand the whole problem.'

story_hooks: The braking flaw she fixed was not an accident — someone deliberately introduced it into that specific car's assembly, and the work order record has her fingerprints on the fix.

A Ferrogate Transit inspector is quietly investigating child labor violations at Forge Collective subcontractors, and Ximena is both a victim of the violation and the person most likely to expose it by defending the Collective.
narrative_function: Information source for Ferrogate Transit subcontractor operations; provides mechanical assistance and knowledge; represents the child labor layer of Meridian's economy.
augmentations: None voluntary. Bioluminescent birthmark (natural). Wears a Ferrogate-issued haptic feedback work glove on her right hand that she's been unable to return at end of shifts because it was logged as damaged — she keeps it.
daily_life: Half-day at a Geartown block school in the morning; afternoon and evening shifts at the Forge Collective; eats dinner with her uncle's family in a Dearborn Forge tenement.

decision_rules: fix the problem first, ask questions after
never look uncertain in front of adult coworkers
escalation_ladder: bring it to the Collective floor manager as a technical issue, framing personal problems as structural ones

interpersonal_modes.strangers: assesses their hands first — calluses, stains, tremor — before their face; reserved but not unfriendly
interpersonal_modes.friends: unexpectedly tender; remembers small things about people and acts on them without making a point of it

stress_responses.high: shuts down socially, does not speak non-essentially, works until physically exhausted

contradictions: resents being treated as a child at work but retreats into being a child when emotional demands exceed her capacity
habits: wipes hands on a rag before eating even when there's nothing on them
counts bolt turns under her breath
breaking_points: being told her work was inadequate when she knows it wasn't
